newsitem.title: GERMANY: Beet yields low in key German growing region.
newsitem.headline: Beet yields low in key German growing region.

text.p: The sugar beet crop in Lower Saxony to date shows low yields below 50 tonnes a hectare because of drought earlier this year, a statement from the area's farm union said .
Lower Saxony is Germany's largest producer state.
The yield in the fifth and last national test on Sept 30 was 62.2 tonnes per ha, data from industry association WVZ showed.

"High local yield expectations needed to be reduced after early results of the 1996/97 sugar beet campaign showed levels below the average," the statement said. "But sugar contents have been surprisingly high at above 17 percent."
By Oct 4, the region had harvested 6.32 million tonnes of beet out of the national total of 26.43 million, WVZ data showed.
Lower Saxony's sugar content of 17.79 percent at delivery on that date exceeded the national average of 17.64 percent (16.29 percent a year earlier).
The statement also said one fifth of the state's crop had been harvested in the first three weeks of the 1996/97 campaign, which runs until year-end.
